proposal.friction: The get_object_info description advertises object_name although its accepted selectors are id or name. In full-catalog document-inspection runs, this misleading guidance produced two failed calls and a retry before successful alternate inspection; it adds avoidable recovery cost without demonstrating a runtime defect.
evidence: Supervisor re-audit: two M2 full-catalog document-inspection calls supplied object_name to get_object_info and returned bare error dictionaries; both are wrong-field calls.

The audit records two observed unknown failed get_object_info calls in workflow-baseline-20260909-235618-5aa1776e-inspect_document-v1, costing 2 calls and 3.327 seconds total, plus one candidate same-intent retry.
The third re-audited bare error was an expected missing-object lookup during recovery and is explicitly excluded from attribution.
The audit is historically heterogeneous and comparison-ineligible, so it supplies discovery evidence only and no measured causal improvement claim.
proposal.hypothesis: A description-only revision that names id and name as accepted selectors, says at least one is required, explains id precedence, and directs agents with no selector to discover objects first will reduce wrong-field get_object_info attempts without changing behavior.
